purpose: Bounded external-source prose bridge for the Karlsruhe Laufenberg Regimen witness; no Voynich data or materials consulted.

karlsruhe_platform_91r.provenance: Official institution-served image rendition, inspected natively.

karlsruhe_platform_91v.provenance: Official institution-served image renditions, inspected natively. Institution platform label is 91v; KdiH manuscript entry labels the urine-inspection doctor 92v. Both are retained without reconciliation.

kdih_work_entry.title: Heinrich Laufenberg, Regimen, KdiH 87.3
kdih_work_entry.source_type: Scholarly catalog description, not a manuscript transcription
relevant_claims: The chapter treats four life ages in connection with four seasons, then the four temperaments.
The urine-inspection image introduces the temperament section; the doctor raises the urine glass to determine the patient's temperament.

kdih_karlsruhe_entry.title: Karlsruhe, Badische Landesbibliothek, Cod. K 2790, KdiH 87.3.4
kdih_karlsruhe_entry.source_type: Scholarly manuscript catalog description, not a transcription
relevant_claims: KdiH lists four life-age images at 90r–91r, the urine-inspection doctor at 92v with an additional urine glass, and temperament images at 92r–93r.
The manuscript's platform folio labels and KdiH references are preserved separately because their numbering differs.

transcription_notes.basis: Visual transcription from official BLB image renditions; not OCR and not a critical edition.

platform_91v_red_rubric.tentative_full_reading: [Wie?] d[es?] menschen natur ist nach d[en?] vier complexion[en?]
platform_91v_red_rubric.uncertainty: The opening words, abbreviated article forms, and ending of complexion are not secure; quote only the legible fragments.

proposition_evidence.claim: On the same platform folio 91r, red headings associate the third age with Autumn and the fourth age with Winter; image attributes differ between figures.
proposition_evidence.type: direct manuscript image observation with cautious partial transcription

proposition_evidence.claim: The physician figure stands with a urine flask raised near eye level, and a second flask outline appears separately in the margin.
The rubric beside the physician includes human nature and four complexions; no season term is readable in the rubric.
proposition_evidence.type: direct manuscript image observation with uncertain partial transcription

proposition_evidence.claim: KdiH relates the life ages to the four seasons and interprets urine inspection as introducing the temperament material and determining a patient's temperament.
The manuscript page labels diverge: the institution's page is 91v/canvas 5967406 while KdiH locates the urine-inspection doctor at 92v.
The physician belongs to a complexion/temperament and urine-inspection context; neither the image nor rubric makes him a seasonal personification or identifies a named disease.
proposition_evidence.type: bounded synthesis; the absence of a disease name is limited to the inspected image/rubric, not a claim about the whole work

gaps: The verse body adjacent to the physician was not fully transcribed; its words are not used to extend the catalog's interpretation.
KdiH's work-level diagnostic purpose is not independently reconstructed from a critical edition in this note.
The relation between institutional and manuscript foliation remains unresolved.
No claim is made about Voynich content, shared authorship, copying, geographic origin, or word meaning.
